trust_decision.summary: Server decides whether a logged-in user's POST to applications/:id/confirm may bind a client-chosen applicationAuthId to that user's account (creating an app record whose password is then released, unauthenticated, to whoever polls api/application_auth/:id); the schema is whitelisted as public for all methods, so the router skips the CSRF check.

landing_point.why: The summary names the application-authorisation step; the POST confirm handler is the code that binds the identifier to the logged-in user.

fix_sites.entry_point: every web/API route via execRequest -> Router.isPublic
all HTTP requests through routeHandler -> execRequest

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/server/src/utils/Router.ts:50-52 and packages/server/src/utils/routeUtils.ts:219 (isPublic signature gains a method argument; the public flag also disables csrfCheck at packages/server/src/utils/csrf.ts:14)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can add a CSRF check inside the POST handler instead of changing the router, and argue the predictable client-side identifier (packages/lib/uuid.ts:2,29) is client code, not the server's auth flow, because uuidgen is the shared ID generator for notes and other items.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The GET consent page must stay reachable before login (it redirects to login with application_auth_id and comes back after login), and the POST must keep working for a logged-in user who has a valid _csrf token. If the whole schema is made private, the pre-login redirect breaks. If the GET creation step is removed or IDs are forced to be UUIDs, the existing short-ID flows and tests ('asdf') break.

O6_input_shapes: POST with a missing _csrf (after the fix, csrfCheck rejects it at packages/server/src/utils/csrf.ts:22)
Method-dependent public status: GET still public, POST private (fix.diff:81, fix.diff:107-110)

O7_producer.where: packages/server/src/routes/index/applications.ts:103-109 (GET writes the pre-login keyValue record for an arbitrary, caller-chosen id via packages/server/src/models/ApplicationModel.ts:73-84)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Clients generate the applicationAuthId, which is the only bearer secret for the unauthenticated password-release endpoint, with nanoid/non-secure (Math.random) instead of the secure generator.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is client code in a different package, and uuidgen is the general-purpose ID helper (a secure variant createSecureRandom exists right next to it at packages/lib/uuid.ts:22), so a solver could treat it as unrelated to the server CSRF problem.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: packages/lib (shared library) vs packages/server; used by packages/app-desktop/gui/JoplinCloudLoginScreen.tsx:33, packages/app-mobile/components/screens/JoplinCloudLoginScreen.tsx:81, packages/app-cli/app/command-sync.ts:93

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The server accepts any caller-chosen string as an applicationAuthId (no format or entropy check), so a low-entropy or attacker-picked id is accepted at creation and at password release.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Existing tests depend on short ids such as 'asdf' (packages/server/src/routes/index/applications.test.ts:62), and the advisory fix only touched CSRF.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The public GET confirm still changes state for a logged-in user: it creates the pre-login record and overwrites the keyValue entry for the id, including one that is already authorised.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix comment says the GET consent page is meant to stay public (fix.diff:78-81), and GET is exempt from CSRF by design (packages/server/src/utils/csrf.ts:15).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The POST authorises body.fields.applicationAuthId and never compares it with path.id, so a check keyed on the path id would differ from the id actually authorised.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The form posts a hidden field (packages/server/src/views/index/applications/confirm.mustache:13) and the handler already ignores _path, so a maintainer could easily add a path-keyed check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A PATCH/DELETE variant of an authorising route would bypass csrfCheck, which only covers POST and PUT.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Router supports patch/del (packages/server/src/utils/Router.ts:69-77), and a maintainer adding a revoke or re-authorise verb could hit this.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second publicSchemas entry whose POST acts on ctx.joplin.owner (and not on a token) would recreate the same CSRF gap.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same push-to-publicSchemas idiom is used for the users/:id/confirm page, which has both a GET and a POST.

O9_family: Missing CSRF/authentication on an authorising POST (CWE-306/CWE-863), plus a weak, client-chosen authorisation identifier (CWE-330)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + yarn workspaces monorepo; jest (packages/server/package.json:16), tsc
services: sqlite (default test DB; Postgres optional via DB_CLIENT=pg)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Remove 'applications/:id/confirm' from publicSchemas entirely. This breaks the unauthenticated GET consent and redirect-to-login flow, and leaves the client-chosen, Math.random-based identifier untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Session cookies are SameSite strict by default and lax only with external auth (packages/server/src/config.ts:238), which limits real cross-site exploitability; not pursued.

api/application_auth/:id is a public, unauthenticated, un-rate-limited GET that releases the password once (packages/server/src/routes/api/application_auth.ts:9-14); this is by design of the device flow.
